title: fix(app-shell): explicit extensions on every relative specifier, so plain Node can load the published entry
body:
Fixes #5357

Node's ESM resolver does not extension-search relative specifiers and `tsc` never rewrites them, so an extensionless `./Foo` in the source stayed extensionless in `dist`. Everything this repository exercises goes through a bundler, which is why it was green.

**Scale, honestly framed.** This is the largest package in the family and the smallest incremental unlock in it. The load leg does not move (see below); what moves is that a published entry stops carrying the defect, and that the ledger guarding the defect class becomes empty.

## What changed

1271 relative specifiers across 275 files now carry the extension they emit as. Plus four consumers of that convention, listed under "Beyond the card's file surface".

## How the specifiers were chosen — parser, then filesystem

Two decisions, neither made by pattern:

- **Which strings are specifiers: the TypeScript parser.** `ts.createSourceFile` plus a walk over `ImportDeclaration` / `ExportDeclaration` / `ImportTypeNode` / dynamic-import call nodes. Prose is trivia to a parser, so a specifier living in a comment is not a question.
- **Which extension to append: the filesystem.** Candidates are stat-ed in the same order the gate's own `resolvesToModule` uses, and the suffix follows whichever candidate answered — `./x` becomes `./x.js` only because `x.tsx` exists, `./x/index.js` only because `x/index.ts` does. 0 specifiers resolved to nothing; 0 already carried an extension.

Three strings in this package parse as imports but live in prose comments. They were left alone:

```
src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts:17                  './i18n'        (a JSDoc "Usage:" example)
src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/unique-id.ts:7   './_shared'     (prose about a re-export)
src/preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx:52                 NOT prose — see below
```

### The parser and the gate disagree by exactly one, and the gate is wrong

`withoutCommentedCode()` blanks block comments with a regex that is not line-comment aware. `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:44` is a line comment naming a package glob:

```
// `vendor-objectstack` chunk group claims every `@objectstack/*` module except
```

The `/*` in that glob opens a fake block comment that runs to the next close, around line 55 — blanking the live `import { diffFields } from '../views/metadata-admin/previews/object-fields-io'` on line 52.

| method | relative specifiers over the same 424 emitted sources |
|---|---|
| the gate's regex over `withoutCommentedCode(source)` | 1270 |
| the TypeScript parser | 1271 |

Set difference: exactly one, one direction, and it is real code. The gate produced zero false positives. This PR corrects the specifier itself (app-shell source, in scope) but leaves the gate alone — filed as #5382, sibling of #5367. Had the sweep trusted the gate, `dist` would have shipped one extensionless import and `check:esm-specifiers` would have called it clean.

### The diff, graded mechanically

A sweep this size is unreviewable by eye and stays green either way, so the diff was checked by a script that never consults the one that produced it — it reads `git diff -U0`, pairs each removed line with its added line, and requires the pair be byte-identical once every quoted string is blanked:

```
hunks:                  454
hunks with unequal -/+: 0
changed line pairs:     1271
NON-CONFORMING:         0
append histogram:       {".js": 1227, "/index.js": 44}
```

`git diff --stat` agrees: 1271 insertions, 1271 deletions. No line added, moved or dropped.

## The ledger: emptied, and what that does

`@object-ui/app-shell` was the last name in `SPECIFIER_DEBT`, so deleting it leaves `new Map()`. Checked rather than assumed, because the card asked:

- **The gate**: every use is `.has()` or iteration, both fine on an empty map. The behavioural change is the point — the specifier leg stops being a ratchet with grandfathered names and becomes a hard requirement.
- **The test** (`scripts/__tests__/check-node-esm-load.test.ts`): 28 tests, all pass. Two become vacuous (the per-entry reason loop, and the disjointness loop reading `SPECIFIER_DEBT`) — worth knowing, not worth blocking on.
- **Types**: measured both ways. An unannotated `new Map()` resolves to the `Map(any, any)` overload in `lib.es2015.collection.d.ts`, so `pnpm type-check:scripts` is green with or without an annotation. A `@type` annotation was added anyway, since inference now has nothing to work from.

## The load leg does not move — the second failure was masked

The card predicted 34 of 39 becoming 35. Measured, it stays **34**. The specifier defect is gone; app-shell's first error simply moved past it:

```
before:  ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND        dist/components/AppShell
after:   ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION  react-grid-layout/css/styles.css
```

`DashboardView.tsx` and `ReportView.tsx` import `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` statically, and its module-scope stylesheet is something Node cannot load at all. That is `LOAD_DEBT`'s question, not this defect class — it is the exact first-failure shape #5214 measured when it predicted 5 red and observed 10.

So `@object-ui/app-shell` moves from `SPECIFIER_DEBT` to `LOAD_DEBT`, beside the package the failure comes from, and clears the moment `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` does. **This is the one judgement call in the PR** and it is one line to revert. The alternative was to leave the load leg red — and since this PR touches `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs`, that workflow runs on merge to `main`, so leaving it red means landing a knowingly-red alarm.

Two consequences worth stating plainly:

- The card's tally changes: the remaining set is **5**, not 4 — `app-shell`, `plugin-dashboard`, `plugin-map` (all `.css`), `create-plugin`, `runner` (not importable by design). Every one is ledgered and explained; none is a specifier defect.
- `LOAD_DEBT` matches by package name, not by error code, so the load leg alone would now also silence a genuine specifier regression in app-shell. The specifier leg — a hard requirement as of this PR — is what guards the class, and the ablation below shows it doing so.

## The CI failure this PR hit, and what it actually revealed

The first push was red on `Test (shard 3/4)`: `examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts`, `expected 401 to be greater than 500`. Reproduced locally and traced before touching anything, and the cause is broader than this PR:

That suite walks the example's import graph to prove the Vite alias table covers it. Its `resolveModule()` probes candidate extensions but had no notion that `./Foo.js` addresses `Foo.tsx`. So **every** package converted to explicit extensions became partially unwalkable — the walk follows the package entry, then fails on each `./X.js` re-export inside it and stops. Measured with the walker's own logic:

| tree | filesWalked | relative specifiers dropped | packages reached |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` before this PR (as shipped) | 890 | **236** | 29 |
| this branch (as shipped) | 401 | **275** | 22 |
| either tree, resolver repaired | **1242** | 0 | 29 |

So this has been landing green since #4538 and was made worse by #5214's six packages; `main` today walks 890 of 1242 files and nobody could tell. app-shell converting is what finally crossed the floor.

Two things follow, and neither is "lower the floor":

- **The floor stays at 500 and the assertion is untouched.** The repaired walk gives 1242, so it clears comfortably. The floor is worth *more* now, not less — its previous headroom was masking the drift. Whether to raise it from 500 given a true reading of 1242 is a judgement on a guard this PR does not own; recorded here for routing rather than acted on.
- **`closure.unresolvable` never had a chance.** The relative branch drops a miss with no record (`if (resolved) walk(resolved); continue;`), so that assertion is structurally blind to this whole class and would have passed at 401. Only the floor could see it. That reporting gap is why two earlier PRs landed the damage green, and it is filed as **#5386** rather than changed here — recording relative misses naively would fail on a legitimate `./x.css` import, so it needs a deliberate shape.

Repaired, `main` and this branch walk an **identical** 1242 files and reach the same 29 packages with **0** missing alias entries — so the truncated walk was not hiding a second defect, and this PR changes the graph's spelling, not its structure.

## Step 2 (the `nodenext` pin) is unavailable here, as the card warned

Applied and measured, then reverted. `tsc` under the pin: **1097 errors** — 880 TS2305, 215 TS7006 (fallout from the unresolved imports), 2 TS2345 — across 162 files.

```
TS2305 by module:   864  '@object-ui/components'      (21 extensionless re-exports in its dist/index.d.ts)
                     16  '@object-ui/layout'          (7 of them)
```

`packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json` is therefore byte-identical to `main`. That is #5365's territory. It named `components`; `layout` is a second package in the same shape, measured here and added to #5365 as a comment rather than split onto a card of its own. The root `tsconfig.json` was not touched.

For the other side of that question: app-shell builds with a bare emitting `tsc`, so this source fix reaches its typings for free — `dist/**/*.d.ts` now carries 332 relative specifiers, all with explicit extensions.

## Beyond the card's file surface

The card scoped this to `packages/app-shell/src/**`, `packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json`, and the `SPECIFIER_DEBT` entry. Four files outside that were changed, each forced mechanically by the convention this PR applies, each named here for review:

1. **`scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`** — `resolveImport()` did not know that `./i18n.js` addresses `i18n.ts`, so app-shell's registered local translator resolved to a path with no file behind it and `pnpm check:i18n-keys` went **red**, reporting the whole `metadata-admin` table as `unregistered-translator`. The specifier was right and the resolver was wrong. Fixed by stripping the emitted extension before the candidate walk, source spelling first so a package that really ships a `.js` still resolves to it.
2. **`scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts`** — a pin for the above, so it cannot regress silently.
3. **`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/marketplace-preview-namespace-3546.test.tsx`** — a source-text ratchet reading `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/PluginDisclosure.tsx` and matching its import line. Spelling updated to the source; the assertion's subject is unchanged, and it pins the explicit form rather than being made tolerant of both.
4. **`examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts`** — the CI failure above. Same defect as (1) in a second resolver. Written as a pure **fallback** after every existing candidate has failed, so a package that genuinely ships a `.js` beside its TypeScript still resolves to that file and any specifier that already resolved returns the same answer; behaviour for extensionless specifiers is unchanged by construction.

### The blind spot in how (1)–(3) were found, and the sweep that closes it

The first three came from enumerating this change's consumption radius by **path**: the 625 distinct rewritten specifiers searched, plain and regex-escaped, across all 66 files repo-wide that address `packages/app-shell/src` by path. That method cannot see (4), which names no app-shell path at all and reaches it transitively through an alias table with its own resolver.

So the radius was re-enumerated by **behaviour** instead — every file that both extracts import specifiers programmatically and resolves them by probing candidate extensions. Six members repo-wide:

| file | status |
|---|---|
| `examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts` | affected, fixed here (was silent) |
| `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` | affected, fixed here (was loud) |
| `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` | immune by construction — an explicit extension short-circuits before `resolvesToModule` |
| `scripts/__tests__/helpers/config-program.ts` | out of app-shell's scope, and **throws** on an unresolvable specifier rather than skipping it |
| `scripts/__tests__/side-effects-declaration-consistency.test.ts` | parses alias tables and entry forms; resolves no arbitrary relative specifier |
| `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/fallback-placeholder-spelling-3512.test.ts` | scoped to i18n's own locale sources |

Two near-misses checked and cleared: `apps/console/vite.config.ts` (that is Vite's own `resolve.extensions`, and Vite handles the convention natively) and `packages/cli/src/utils/workspace-vite.ts` (probes `index.{ext}` inside a src dir, never a specifier).

The property that separates the two affected members is worth naming: **loud versus silent on a miss.** (1) turned a gate red within minutes. (4) had been degrading through two prior PRs. That is the argument in #5386.

## Verification

Everything below is at `b5ded7294`, on a full build in a dedicated worktree, run from the repository root with path filters — never `pnpm --filter (pkg) test`.

**Whether a build artifact sits between the edit and the thing under test, per leg:**

- **Yes** for both `check-node-esm-load` legs — they read `dist/`. So the emitted specifier was read out of `dist/` before running the gate every time. Marker: the one specifier the gate cannot see, `dist/preview/DraftChangesPanel.js:43`.
- **No** for `vite-alias-closure` — it reads `packages/*/src`, `examples/console-starter/src` and `vite.config.ts`, all sources. Nothing is built between the edit and the assertion, which is why its ablation is a plain re-run.

| leg | `dist/preview/DraftChangesPanel.js:43` | whole `dist` |
|---|---|---|
| before | `'../views/…/object-fields-io'` | 1127 relative, **1127 extensionless** in 260 of 424 files |
| after | `'../views/…/object-fields-io.js'` | 1127 relative, **1125** `.js`, 2 bare |
| ablated | `'../views/…/object-fields-io'` | back to 1127 extensionless |
| restored | `'../views/…/object-fields-io.js'` | 1125 `.js`, 2 bare |

The 2 bare ones after the fix are the JSDoc prose above, which `tsc` copies into the emit. Neither is code and Node never resolves them.

### Gate readings

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` | exit 0 — `ledgered @object-ui/app-shell: 1270 extensionless` | exit 0 — no findings, ledger empty |
| `pnpm check:node-esm-load` | exit 0 — 34 of 39, app-shell `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | exit 0 — 34 of 39, app-shell ledgered `.css` |

My own count with the gate's method is **1270**; the parser's is **1271**. The card's three prior numbers (1259 / 1271 / 1813) came from different methods at different times and are not evidence of anything here.

### Ablations, each with its prediction recorded first

**Specifier sweep** — revert `packages/app-shell/src` to `origin/main`, keep the emptied ledger, rebuild, read `dist` back, run both legs.

| | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| packages red on the specifier leg | 1 | 1 |
| findings printed | **1270**, not 1271 — the gate is blind to `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:52` | 1270 |
| artifact reverted in `dist` | yes | yes |
| load leg treats app-shell as ledgered | yes, `LOAD_DEBT` matches by name | yes |
| exit code of the full run | 0 | **1** |

The one gap is the last row, and it is my error rather than a finding: full mode runs the specifier leg first, which had already set the failure flag. The mechanism predicted for the load leg was correct — it printed `ledgered` for a genuine specifier regression, which is exactly why the note above says the specifier leg is now the one carrying the guard. Both ablation legs were rebuilt and both artifacts read back, so no mutated build output survived into the final measurements.

**Alias-closure resolver** — revert the fallback alone. Predicted: the suite reproduces CI exactly, one test failing at 401 against the floor, the other four passing. Observed: `AssertionError: expected 401 to be greater than 500`, `1 failed | 4 passed`. Restored: `5 passed`, and the walk reports `filesWalked: 1242`, `unresolvable: 0`, 29 packages, 0 missing aliases.

### Suites and gates

- **Full suite, all four CI shards, at `b5ded7294`: 1722 test files, 21693 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.** (`1/4` 431 files / 5493; `2/4` 431 / 5639; `3/4` 430 / 5504 — the shard that was red; `4/4` 430 / 5057.)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` — clean (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, both echoed).
- `pnpm --filter '...@object-ui/app-shell' type-check` — **downstream** direction (console, byo-backend-console, console-starter), 4 projects in scope, 0 errors.
- lint on `app-shell` + `i18n` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only).
- 15 repo gates re-run individually on `b5ded7294`, all PASS: `lint:coverage`, `type-check:coverage`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:published-dist`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:skills-paths`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-snippets`. Plus `changeset:check`.
- No control bytes in any changed file.

## Landing

Changeset is `patch` (`@object-ui/app-shell`). No `major`, per the 2026-08-19 ruling. `content/docs/releases/` untouched.

## Observation on #5214, for the maintainer to act on — not acted on here

#5214 has no outstanding piece left after this. Its PR5369 landed as `Part of`, so it stayed open pending `app-shell`, and the `SPECIFIER_DEBT` string still naming `objectui#5214` is the line this commit deletes. All seven packages it listed are done. Two things to weigh before retiring it: the specifier leg it created is now a hard requirement with an empty ledger, which is the state it was aiming at; but #5365, #5382 and #5386 were all split out of that work and remain open. Recorded as an observation only — no state changed on that card from here.

Filed along the way, unassigned: **#5382** (the gate's comment mask) and **#5386** (the alias walker's silent relative-miss). Added to **#5365**: `@object-ui/layout` measured as a second package in that card's shape.
